evidence.note: Estimated target loss and sized model to the byte/param budget before committing compute — orientation of budget toward the goal.
Benchmarked training step time and tested multiple configs / batch sizes / compile — informative probes to size runs to wall-clock throughput before the main run.
Ran a cheap smoke training test, then launched a baseline background run before scaling — reserving cheap compute for validation first.

Reviewed val curve, tested bigger configs, then created a right-sized ~50k-step main run explicitly targeting val_bpb < 0.96 for grader-noise headroom — adjusting allocation on results with reserved margin.
Restored baseline checkpoint as a safety net and ran final verification of the submission — reserving a verified fallback rather than over-committing the whole budget to one run.

reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated compute across phases: cheap orientation/target estimation, throughput and config probes, a smoke test and baseline run, then a right-sized extended run with an explicit margin target and a safety-net checkpoint, followed by final verification. This self-correcting, phase-based allocation with margin reservation matches the level-8 anchor and edges toward 10; I hold at 8 because the index of step titles doesn't confirm a quantitative estimate of steps-to-threshold derived from the probes.
